description: The minimum architecture a reader needs to place the numbers: one host (its CPU, RAM and power supplies), four RTX 3090 Founders Edition cards in two NVLink pairs, each pair passed whole to its own VM. The motherboard, the hypervisor and its version, the guest OS, host names, addresses, VM ids, storage and network layout are deliberately left out.
evidence_note: 'rig description' is the lab's own server notes and board diagram (not published); each fact above was transcribed from them and checked against them by the exporter.

facts.fact: One host with four RTX 3090 Founders Edition cards, 24 GB each.
The four cards form two NVLink pairs, each joined by a 4-slot NVLink bridge between physically adjacent slots.
Inside each VM, nvidia-smi reports the pair's link as NV4: 4 links at 14.062 GB/s each, about 56 GB/s in each direction.
One card's link was read on the host at 16 GT/s x16 (PCIe 4.0), in a slot wired to the CPU, on 2026-09-25. The links of the other cards are not recorded.
Each NVLink pair is passed through whole (PCIe passthrough) to its own VM, called pair A and pair B here; each VM has 8 vCPU and 64 GB of RAM.
Each GPU VM runs the NVIDIA driver 580.173.02 (CUDA 13.0).
Each card runs at its stock 350 W power limit (nvidia-smi showed a card reaching it during a fine-tuning run).
Stock RTX 3090 Founders Edition cards: the Founders Edition has no dual BIOS.
The host's CPU is one AMD EPYC 7F52 (16 cores, 32 threads); each pair's VM gets 8 vCPU of it.
The host has 256 GB of ECC DDR4 (8 × 32 GB DDR4-3200 RDIMM, eight channels); each pair's VM gets 64 GB of it, which is where the part of a model that does not fit in VRAM goes.
Two power supplies feed the host and its four cards: a Corsair HX1500i and a Corsair HX1000i, started together by a dual-PSU adapter. Which unit powers which card is not recorded here.

not_recorded: the PCIe link width and speed of three of the four cards
